record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: Let G be a countably compact topological group such that every closed subgroup of G is separable, and let H be a topological group with a countable network. Must every closed subgroup of the product group G x H be separable?

evidence.quote: Let G be a countably compact topological group such that all closed subgroups of G are separable, and H a topological group with a countable network. Are the closed subgroups of G x H separable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that a topological space is separable if it contains a countable dense subset, and is countably compact if every countable open cover has a finite subcover (equivalently, every infinite subset has an accumulation point). A network for a topological space X is a family N of subsets of X such that for every point x ∈ X and every open neighborhood U of x there exists N ∈ N with x ∈ N ⊆ U; the space has a countable network if such a family N can be chosen countable.

Let G be a countably compact topological group with the property that every closed subgroup of G is separable, and let H be a topological group that admits a countable network. Endow the product group G × H with the product topology and the coordinatewise group operation.

Question: must every closed subgroup of G × H be separable?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a recent survey on separability of topological groups as an explicitly stated open problem. Related results show positive answers in special cases (e.g., when H is separable metrizable) and negative answers for products of two countably compact CSS groups under MA¬CH, but no resolution of the specific question (countably compact G with CSS, H with countable network) was found in the literature search.

status_evidence.title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on separability of products of topological groups, including the case of countably compact groups multiplied by groups with a countable network.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed as an open problem in this survey on separability of topological groups.

status_evidence.title: Topological groups whose closed subgroups are separable, and the product operation
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when the class CSS (closed subgroups separable) is preserved under products; provides positive partial results and consistency-based counterexamples for products of two countably compact CSS groups.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist but the specific case of a countably compact CSS group times a group with countable network is not resolved.
